children: will acquire Alif Semiconductor in an all-cash transaction for $1.35 billion, both companies said on Wednesday.
The deal will help expand Analog Devices’ total addressable market across industrial, data center infrastructure, defense, energy, robotics, and digital health, among others, the companies

"By combining Alif's digital processing capabilities with our leadership in multi-modal sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity, and software, we can empower customers to create entirely new classes of secure, intelligent systems that sense, reason, and act locally in real time. This is the next frontier of AI: embodied and deterministic. This is Physical Intelligence in action," said ADI CEO Vincent Roche.
As part of the deal, Analog Devices may pay an incremental contingent consideration of up to $200 million.
California-based Alif Semiconductor is a provider of power-efficient EdgeAI microcontrollers and fusion processors.
The transaction is expected to close before the end of the calendar year 2026, the companies said.

Shares of Wilmington, Massachusetts-based Analog Devices, which provides semiconductors to businesses in various of ​industries, including ⁠aerospace, automotive, and communications, were down over 1% in premarket trading.

The deal comes as the artificial intelligence market is experiencing intense competition driven by heavy capital investments from organisations. Earlier in May, Analog Devices acquired AI ​chip company Empower Semiconductor in an all-cash transaction for $1.5 billion.

title: Analog Devices to Buy Alif Semiconductor for $1.35B cash
